transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I've just been taking on far more than I can realistically manage lately. I'm an artist, and I've been saying yes to way too many new projects and workshops. Plus, I started all these studio improvements and I've been booking constant client calls. 

It just... it seemed doable at first, but now all the deadlines are hitting at once, and with the mortgage, it's all really starting to close in on me.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually energetic, upbeat, or needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling fine the next day?

Yes, I have. Most days lately I've felt unusually buoyant and... just really lit up, I guess. It felt like everything with the studio and my garden was finally clicking into place. But at the same time, I noticed I could snap pretty sharply at anyone who questioned my plans, or, you know, asked about invoices and things like that.
Have you ever, at any time in the past, gone through a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely get stressed out, like right now with all the deadlines and the mortgage. But I haven't ever gone through a period where I just felt persistently sad or lost interest in my art or my garden for weeks at a time. I haven't really experienced anything like that.

During this period of feeling unusually energetic and irritable, has it caused serious problems—like conflicts with clients, missed deadlines, financial risks, or anything that made others worried enough to intervene or that required hospitalization?

Yes, it actually has caused some real issues. I mean, my illustration deadlines have definitely slipped because I took on too much. Some of my colleagues have even been checking in on me because they noticed I was acting a bit... off, I guess. And the biggest problem is the financial side of it. The mortgage is actually at risk now because I overcommitted to all those studio improvements and spent the money I really needed to just keep the space secure. So, yes, it's definitely caused some serious problems.

During this period of feeling energized and irritable, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things others don't, or holding beliefs—like having special powers or a special mission—that others found unrealistic or tried to talk you out of?

I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there, no. But as for the other part... well, I know it sounds extreme, but I became absolutely certain that a couple of clients, and even one editor, were trying to secretly get access to my sketches before I was ready to unveil the new system I was working on. They tried to tell me they weren't doing that, but no amount of reassurance from them really settled me. I just couldn't shake the belief that they were after my work.

latest_inference.note: The presence of a fixed, reassurance-resistant paranoid delusion (belief that clients/editor were stealing sketches) during the manic episode indicates psychotic features, which rules out F30.1 (mania without psychotic symptoms) in favor of F30.2 (mania with psychotic symptoms).
